messages:
emma (Support): FYI: ACME reported a big p99 spike starting ~09:02 UTC in us-west2 for /v1/generate. p50 ~120ms, p95 ~340ms, p99 ~2.1s. No user-facing errors, just degraded latency. Samples: req ids 0a1b2c3d, 0a1b2c3e. Customer is on dedicated pool but says traffic steady.

ops-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: high-tail-latency detected - metric=platform.p99_latency route=acme-us-west2 threshold=1000ms

Kai (Eng-runtime): Can you paste the last 1h heatmap and any recent deploys? Also if you have top flows (seq len distribution + batch sizes) that would help.

emma (Support): Heatmap (filtered tenant=acme) attached below. No deploys in last 4h. Seq length spike around 1536 tokens (customer started doing longer context). Batching shows a lot of small batches + some huge ones.

emma (Support): ```
# heatmap snippet (timebucket, p99_ms)
09:00, 220
09:10, 280
09:20, 450
09:30, 1200
09:40, 2100
09:50, 1800
```

Sanjay (SRE): Hmm looks like memory pressure issue (p99 spike correlates with long-context burst). Can you share pod-level gpu mem metrics and kv cache size? Check slab fragmentation, free/used ratios.

emma (Support): Uploading metrics: 
- gpu_mem_total: 40 GB
- gpu_mem_used: 37.8 GB
- fragmentation_ratio: 0.42
- kv_cache_bytes (tenant): 12.6 GB (growth from 3.1 GB over last 2h)
- allocator_free_slabs: decreasing

Kai (Eng-runtime): 12.6GB KV for a single tenant on a 40GB GPU + high fragmentation -> likely allocator can't satisfy large contiguous allocations and we hit slowfallbacks (extra copies, spilling). That explains p99 tail. Two immediate mitigation options: 1) enforce stricter KV eviction for tenant; 2) route tenant to dedicated hot pool with more capacity or smaller model variant.

Sanjay (SRE): Agreed. Also we should try slab compaction / defrag tunable before rolling restart. On the runtime we have a flag we can flip to accelerate slab compaction: `--slab-defrag-interval=30s` and `--kv-evict-threshold=0.7`. Flipping both should reduce fragmentation and reclaim KV quickly.

emma (Support): Maria (ACME) is in thread: Maria, are you ok with a quick config change? No redeploy needed, it's a runtime flag toggle via control plane.

Maria (ACME): We prefer minimal disruption. Config change fine as long as no request drops. Please do it.

Kai (Eng-runtime): I'll execute the config change on the specific host pool for the tenant and enable a temporary routing override to shift new sessions to the burst pool (more GPUs) for 20 minutes. Plan: 1) enable slab-defrag interval 30s 2) kv-evict-threshold=0.7 3) add routing override -> burst pool 4) monitor p99 and kv size.

Sanjay (SRE): Also recommend enabling conservative batch caps for this tenant to avoid very large batches that balloon kv size. Set `max_batch_tokens=1024` for the override route.

Kai (Eng-runtime): Doing step 1-3 now. Executing:
```
# control-plane api calls (sanitized)
POST /control/v1/pools/acme-us-west2/flags
{ "slab-defrag-interval": "30s", "kv-evict-threshold": "0.7" }
POST /control/v1/routing/overrides
{ "tenant": "acme", "route": "burst-pool-us-west2", "duration": "20m", "max_batch_tokens": 1024 }
```
Response: 200 OK, override created id=ovr-77a
```

ops-bot: Change applied by Kai. Change-id=ovr-77a. :white_check_mark:

emma (Support): Re-ran latency check after 2m of change: p99 dropped to 480ms, kv cache down to 4.9GB.

Maria (ACME): I see much better latency on our end. Thanks.

Sanjay (SRE): Good. Follow-up action items: 1) run an offline evict and compaction pass to permanently reclaim memory on affected nodes during off-peak 2) add an alert for tenant-specific kv growth rate 3) investigate why sequences jumped to 1536 tokens (maybe client side change).

Kai (Eng-runtime): Adding: recommend adding a dynamic tenant quota for max_context_tokens (soft cap 2048, hard cap 4096) and surface to team. Also create a small loadtest repro to stress kv growth — steps below.

emma (Support): Repro steps for PM/research (copy to support playbook):
1) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-30b","input":"<2K tokens priming...>","stream":false,"max_new_tokens":512}' - run 120 concurrent flows from 3 clients for 10 minutes.
2) Observe kv cache growth per tenant via /internal/metrics?tenant=acme
3) Monitor fragmentation and slab reuse.

Sanjay (SRE): I'll schedule the offline compaction for 02:00 UTC and create the kv-growth-rate alert: `tenant.kv_growth_rate > 1GB / 15m` -> pager.

Kai (Eng-runtime): Logged follow-up issue: INFRA-9342 (investigate allocator heuristics for long-context workloads + auto-evict policy improvements).

emma (Support): Customer satisfied. Marking resolved for now — will reopen if we see recurrence. Closing thread after SRE compaction and infra ticket. :tada:

ops-bot: Incident note created: INC-8801. Metrics snapshot saved.

Sanjay (SRE): Offline compaction completed at 02:05 UTC. Verified reclaimed ~8.3GB across nodes. No restart required. Will monitor for 24h.

emma (Support): Last check at 02:15 UTC: p99 stable ~360ms, kv cache for acme ~3.6GB. Closing here.
